title: Game Day Plan: Quantization Profile Rollback Drill (Route Disable + Global Kill-Switch)
content:
Doc purpose
This game day simulates a production-like regression caused by enabling a Quantization Profile on a single route, then exercises (1) route-level disable and (2) global kill-switch activation. The goal is to ensure SRE + Platform + Runtime can detect the issue quickly, coordinate cleanly, roll back deterministically, and verify recovery via dashboards/logs/audit trails.

Scope
- In scope:
  - Route-level quantization_profile_ref disable for one route
  - Global kill-switch to disable quantization profiles platform-wide
  - Verification steps: fallback_rate, error rate, p95 latency, and request log annotations (quant_profile_id + applied/fallback/disabled)
  - Comms + incident hygiene (timeline, decision points, audit checks)
- Out of scope:
  - Changing/republishing model registry artifacts during the drill
  - Full customer comms process (we’ll do internal comms only)

Environment
- Primary: perf-canary (preferred) or prod-sim dedicated slice if perf-canary is unavailable
- Affected deployment modes to validate:
  - Hosted (control plane + routing + runtime)
  - Dedicated (at least one dedicated cluster that mirrors prod policy evaluation)

Participants + roles
- Incident Commander (IC): Connor O’Brien (SRE)
- Deputy IC / Comms: Aisha Bello (SRE)
- Ops Scribe: Dev Patel (Support escalation lead, acting as scribe)
- Platform / Control Plane: Ethan Park
- Routing / Policy: Mina Haddad
- Runtime: Noah Patel
- Applied ML / Quality: Selene Huang (observe quality signals; validate guardrails are behaving)
- Console / Audit visibility (observer): Chloe Martin
- Security / Audit requirements (observer): Naomi Feldman
- Quant profiles SME (observer): Arjun Desai

Pre-req checklist (must be green 24h before)
1) Feature flag eligibility
- Route-level quantization controls available in the environment
- Kill-switch is wired through policy + runtime for this environment

2) Drill route + baseline
- Identify one route to use as “drill-route” (non-customer-facing; synthetic traffic OK)
- Confirm drill-route currently has quantization disabled (default behavior) and is stable for at least 30 minutes

3) Dashboards pinned + links shared
- Quant profile rollout dashboard panels:
  - enabled_rate by route
  - fallback_rate by route/model
  - p95 latency (prefill vs decode if available)
  - 5xx / error rate
  - cost/token proxy panel (optional)
- Runtime logs/traces filter:
  - request_id
  - quant_profile_id
  - resolution_outcome = applied | fallback | disabled

4) Alerting config
- Temporary alert thresholds enabled for drill window:
  - fallback_rate > 2% sustained 5 min (warning)
  - 5xx rate > 1% sustained 5 min (page in real prod; for drill, notify in channel)
  - p95 decode latency +20% vs baseline sustained 10 min

5) Permissions
- Confirm who can:
  - update route config (Ethan / Mina)
  - activate kill-switch (IC + SRE on-call perms)
  - view audit logs (Chloe / Naomi)

6) Traffic generator
- Synthetic load for drill-route:
  - steady 20–50 RPS with representative context lengths
  - at least 2 distributions: short prompts (<=1k tokens) and long prompts (>=6k tokens)

Comms plan
- Primary channel: #eng-sre (game day thread)
- Secondary: #eng-platform, #eng-runtime, #eng-ml (observers)
- One shared doc for timeline capture: this document + scribe notes appended
- Call bridge: Zoom “SRE War Room” (link posted 10 minutes prior)

Safety constraints (hard stops)
- If drill environment instability impacts shared infra (registry load, control plane errors), stop immediately.
- If we observe cross-route impact (routes not in drill scope), stop and revert to baseline.
- No changes to production customer routes.

Drill scenario overview
We will simulate an “enable quant profile causes regression” event in two variants:
A) Latency regression: enabling a specific profile increases decode p95 and triggers fallback behavior in some cases.
B) Quality regression signal: simulated by forcing a “quality guardrail alert” entry (or using a known failing prompt-set signal in perf-canary) to drive the decision to roll back.

We will execute route-level disable first. If metrics do not recover within the target window (or if impact is broader than expected), we escalate to global kill-switch.

Success criteria
- Time-to-detect (TTD): <= 10 min from regression injection to acknowledgement in channel
- Time-to-mitigate (TTM):
  - Route-level disable applied within 10 min of decision
  - Global kill-switch applied within 10 min of escalation decision
- Verification:
  - enabled_rate for drill-route returns to 0
  - runtime logs show resolution_outcome=disabled for new requests
  - fallback_rate returns to baseline within 15 min
  - p95 latency returns within 10% of baseline within 20 min
- Auditability:
  - Audit event(s) present for route config change and kill-switch change, with actor + diff + timestamp
- No collateral impact:
  - No elevated errors on non-drill routes; no registry thundering herd

Detailed run-of-show (timing)
All times in PT. Total duration: 90 minutes.

T-15 (09:45) — Pre-brief
- IC reviews goals, safety constraints, roles.
- Confirm dashboards open and traffic generator running.
- Record baseline metrics snapshot (scribe): p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, fallback_rate, enabled_rate.

T0 (10:00) — Start
- Post “Game Day Start” message in #eng-sre with participants and drill-route id.

T+5 (10:05) — Inject regression (Route-level enable)
- Platform/Routing enables quantization_profile_ref for drill-route.
- Pick a profile that is valid/compatible but expected to shift latency OR a pre-selected “stress” profile in perf-canary.
- Scribe records exact change:
  - route id/name
  - previous quantization setting
  - new quant_profile_ref
  - actor

T+10 (10:10) — Observe + triage
- IC prompts: “What changed? What signals confirm it’s quant profile related?”
- Runtime validates logs include quant_profile_id and applied outcomes.
- Routing validates policy resolution results and any incompatibility fallback paths.
- Applied ML observer notes any quality signal (if available) and confirms guardrails threshold policy reference.

Expected signals (depending on scenario)
- Increased p95 decode latency
- Increased fallback_rate (policy rejects some requests due to seq length/hardware constraints)
- Potential elevated 5xx due to profile metadata fetch retries (if misconfigured caching)

T+20 (10:20) — Decision point #1: Route-level rollback
- IC asks for recommendation from Platform/Routing/Runtime.
- Execute route-level disable: set quantization_profile_ref to default/none for drill-route.
- Scribe records:
  - decision time
  - command/API used
  - expected propagation time

T+25 to T+40 (10:25–10:40) — Verify recovery
- Verify via dashboards:
  - enabled_rate -> 0 on drill-route
  - p95 latency trending back to baseline
  - fallback_rate trending down
- Verify via logs/traces:
  - new requests show resolution_outcome=disabled
  - quant_profile_id absent or set to “none” depending on logging standard

T+40 (10:40) — Inject “stuck impact” to force escalation (optional but recommended)
Choose ONE escalation technique (pre-approved, low risk):
1) Introduce a second route (drill-route-2) already enabled with quant profile to simulate “multiple routes impacted”, OR
2) Simulate a policy cache issue (toggle a config cache TTL lower) to increase incompatibility/fallback signals, OR
3) Announce “quality regression alert fired” as if from guardrails (tabletop injection) requiring broader rollback.

T+45 (10:45) — Decision point #2: Global kill-switch
- IC asks: “Is route-level rollback sufficient? If not, why? What is the blast radius?”
- If escalating, IC executes global kill-switch activation.
- Platform/Routing confirms kill-switch propagation to policy resolution.
- Runtime confirms kill-switch effect: quant profiles not applied even if route config still references a profile.

T+50 to T+65 (10:50–11:05) — Verify kill-switch effect
- Verify across routes:
  - enabled_rate may still show configured refs, but applied outcome should be disabled globally
  - fallback_rate should approach 0 attributable to quant profiles
- Verify logs:
  - resolution_outcome=disabled_global (or equivalent) if implemented
- Confirm registry fetch traffic returns to normal (avoid replay of prior thundering herd incident pattern).

T+70 (11:10) — Restore normal state
- Deactivate global kill-switch.
- Keep drill-route quantization disabled.
- Confirm steady state for 10 minutes.

T+80 (11:20) — Debrief
- What went well / what was confusing?
- Any missing dashboards, unclear metric names, or ambiguous runbook steps?
- Did we have deterministic confirmation that the profile was or wasn’t applied?

T+90 (11:30) — Close
- IC posts summary + action items.
- Scribe attaches timeline and key screenshots/links.

Execution details (how-to)
Note: Use the approved runbook steps; below is a checklist summary so the team doesn’t hunt during the drill.

Route-level disable checklist
1) Identify route id and current quantization_profile_ref.
2) Update route config: quantization_profile_ref = "default" (or null per API contract).
3) Confirm audit log event emitted for the route change.
4) Confirm policy engine resolves “disabled” for route.
5) Confirm runtime logs show resolution_outcome=disabled for new requests.

Global kill-switch checklist
1) Activate kill-switch (platform config): quant_profiles_global_disable = true.
2) Confirm audit log event emitted for kill-switch change.
3) Confirm policy engine evaluation returns “globally disabled” outcome.
4) Confirm runtime refuses to apply profiles even if route references them.
5) Monitor for unintended side effects:
   - increased latency due to mode switch
   - errors due to config propagation
   - registry fetch anomalies

Verification queries (copy/paste into notes)
- “Show me evidence for request_id=___ that the profile was applied or not applied.”
- “In the last 5 minutes, what % of drill-route requests had quant_profile_id set?”
- “Is fallback_rate driven by incompatibility checks or runtime failures?”

Artifacts to capture during drill
- Baseline metric snapshot (pre-injection)
- Metric snapshot at peak regression
- Time of rollback change + time metrics recovered
- 3 example request_ids showing:
  - applied (before rollback)
  - disabled (after route rollback)
  - disabled due to kill-switch (after escalation)
- Audit log entries for both changes

Risks + mitigations
- Risk: Registry metadata fetch spike / retries cause infra noise.
  - Mitigation: keep traffic generator capped; confirm caching/rate-limit protections are enabled; stop if control plane error rate rises.
- Risk: Confusion between “configured” vs “applied” states.
  - Mitigation: require log/tracing proof (resolution_outcome) as source of truth; highlight this in debrief.
- Risk: Permissions delay.
  - Mitigation: pre-validate RBAC; have backup operator for kill-switch.

Post-drill follow-ups (action items template)
- [ ] Update rollback runbook with any missing steps or clarified verification.
- [ ] Fix any ambiguous metric names or add missing panels.
- [ ] Confirm audit log exporter includes: quant_profile_id, route id, actor, diff.
- [ ] If kill-switch propagation was slow/unclear, file perf/consistency ticket.
- [ ] If route-level disable didn’t recover within SLO, create bug with timeline + request_ids.

Appendix: Notes for scribe (fill during drill)
- Start time:
- Drill route id/name:
- Profile enabled (ref/version):
- Baseline metrics (p95 latency, 5xx, fallback_rate):
- Peak metrics:
- Decision time (route rollback):
- Rollback executed by:
- Recovery time:
- Decision time (kill-switch):
- Kill-switch executed by:
- Kill-switch verification proof (links/request_ids):
